requirements.quote:
address validation implicit in the handshake ensures that -- for a
   new connection -- a client will not send other types of packets to a
   destination that does not understand QUIC or is not willing to accept
   a QUIC connection.
requirements.condition: For a new connection, when the destination does not understand QUIC or is unwilling to accept a QUIC connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client sends packet types other than Initial packets to that destination before handshake address validation permits doing so.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can use a non-QUIC or unwilling destination and verify that the client sends no non-Initial packet types during establishment.

requirements.quote:
by clients.  A client choosing an unpredictable Destination
   Connection ID ensures that servers are unable to control any of the
   encrypted portion of Initial packets from clients.
requirements.condition: When a client chooses the Destination Connection ID for an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Destination Connection ID is unpredictable so that a server cannot control any encrypted portion of the client's Initial packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Choosing a server-predictable Destination Connection ID that enables server control over encrypted Initial-packet content.
requirements.why_checkable: The client's Destination Connection ID generation and whether server-selected inputs can predict or control it can be tested or inspected.

requirements.quote: Clients, however, are not obligated to use the NEW_TOKEN frame.
requirements.condition: When a client has received a NEW_TOKEN frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treating use of the token from NEW_TOKEN as mandatory client behavior.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can verify that a client is permitted to establish a connection without using a received NEW_TOKEN token.

requirements.quote:
Request forgery attacks that rely on the Token field can be avoided
   if clients send an empty Token field when the server address has
   changed from when the NEW_TOKEN frame was received.
requirements.condition: When the server address differs from the address in use when the NEW_TOKEN frame was received.
requirements.required_behavior: Send an empty Token field to avoid Token-field request forgery.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the previously supplied NEW_TOKEN token at the changed server address when applying this mitigation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can change the server address after receipt of NEW_TOKEN and inspect whether the next Initial packet contains an empty Token field.

requirements.quote:
Sending a Retry packet (Section 17.2.5) offers a server the option to
   change the Token field.  After sending a Retry, the server can also
   control the Destination Connection ID field of subsequent Initial
   packets from the client.
requirements.condition: After a server sends a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Subsequent client Initial packets use the Token field and Destination Connection ID selected through the Retry exchange.
requirements.why_checkable: A server can send a Retry containing chosen token and connection-ID values and inspect the client's subsequent Initial packet fields.

requirements.quote:
Retry packet validates the server's address, thereby preventing the
   use of subsequent Initial packets for request forgery.
requirements.required_behavior: The server's address is validated before subsequent Initial packets are usable.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using subsequent Initial packets for request forgery through an unvalidated server address.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused Retry test can verify address validation state before subsequent Initial packets are accepted or generated.
